output: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany has criticized UEFA's Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, arguing that they protect established clubs, not prevent teams from bankruptcy. Last year, City were fined £50million and ordered to limit their transfer spending due to FFP breaches, while rivals Manchester United were able to spend £150m despite being £400m in debt. Kompany believes FFP hampers smaller clubs' ability to challenge the established elite, stating that City's success is due to their owners' investments and the subsequent fan growth and revenue increase. He emphasized the positive impact of City's owners on the community and Manchester's economy.

Bath Rugby has signed England Sevens international Jeff Williams, who will join the team for the upcoming season. The 26-year-old, who has played for various clubs including Hamiltons in Cape Town and France, is renowned for his 36 tries on the World Series circuit and his contribution to England's victory at the Tokyo Sevens this month. Both Bath coach Mike Ford and England Sevens head coach Simon Amor are optimistic about Williams' dynamism and potential to contribute to the team's attacking style of play.

The article announces that Jared Leto has been cast as the Joker in the 2016 film "Suicide Squad," marking his first appearance as the character on the big screen since Heath Ledger. Notably, there is no Batman present in the film. Leto significantly transformed his appearance for the role, shaving his face and cutting his hair, fully committing to the iconic villainous character. The movie, also starring Will Smith, Margot Robbie, and various other villains and anti-heroes, is set to hit theaters on August 5, 2016.

Three Florida corrections officers and a former officer trainee have been charged with conspiring to murder a former inmate, following an undercover FBI operation. The men, who are reportedly members of a KKK group, allegedly sought revenge after the inmate fought with one of them. The FBI staged a fake crime scene to convince the suspects that the murder had been carried out, and they are now facing up to 30 years in prison if found guilty. Florida Attorney General Pam Bondi denounced the violent actions rooted in prejudice.

Manny Pacquiao's conference call discussing his upcoming fight against Floyd Mayweather was abruptly canceled due to technical difficulties, caused by a large number of boxing journalists and broadcasters participating in the call. Pacquiao could only answer one question, and the rescheduled call will be held at a later date. American boxer Floyd Mayweather is scheduled to have his own conference call on Wednesday.

The Miami Open celebrates notable milestones with grand cake presentations, with Serena Williams being the latest recipient for recording her 700th career victory. Andy Murray also received such a cake after winning his 500th match. Williams progressed to the semi-finals by beating Sabine Lisicki in a tight match, setting up a clash with Simona Halep, who defeated Sloane Stephens to book her place. Williams's hopes of meeting sister Venus were squashed when Venus was defeated by Carla Suarez Navarro.

Beijing International Airport, also known as Daxing Airport, is set to launch the world's largest terminal, Terminal 1, in 2018, to accommodate rising numbers of Chinese tourists traveling the world. The terminal, designed by British-Iraqi architect Zaha Hadid, will span 700,000 square metres and is expected to handle 45 million passengers annually.

2. The terminal's six-tier design aims to minimize walking distances and increase connectivity, featuring large open spaces and a central courtyard as a meeting point for global travelers. The design reflects the harmony and balance between Chinese landscape and culture, creating a feeling of spaciousness and openness to welcome visitors to Beijing.

3. As the second busiest international airport in the world, Daxing Airport saw 109 million Chinese tourists in 2014, spending $164 billion, marking a significant increase from the 10 million outbound tourists in 2000. The new terminal is predicted to facilitate this continued increase in global tourism due to China's growing influence on the worldwide stage.

1. Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal revealed that Wayne Rooney suffered a knee injury during their Premier League loss against Everton on Sunday, with Robin van Persie replacing him in the final minutes.
2. The England international was withdrawn due to the injury, which now has an unknown severity, leaving United fourth in the race for automatic Champions League qualification.
3. The loss, compounded by Rooney's injury, has potentially opened the door for Liverpool to exert pressure on United's position in the standings, with crucial upcoming matches scheduled against West Brom, Crystal Palace, Arsenal, and Hull.

1. Manchester City is reportedly interested in signing Arsenal midfielder Jack Wilshere, but he is recovering from ankle surgery and hasn't yet returned to the first team.

2. On a day off, Wilshere shared an Instagram post showcasing his shopping trip, which included food such as Seriously Fruity Mixed Berry Crisp cereal, Special K Oats and Honey, eggs, baked beans, and corn on the cob.

3. Wilshere asked for help from his social media followers to put away the groceries, jokingly complaining about the task. His posts hinted at a love for cereal and a disciplined approach to nutrition as part of his fitness routine.

A Venezuelan woman named Marleni Olivo threw a mango with her phone number and a message at President Nicolas Maduro to request a new apartment, an act she said was meant to toss a note as others in the crowd were doing. In a surprising turn of events, Maduro responded by announcing on live TV that Olivo would receive a new apartment as part of the Great Housing Mission of Venezuela. Despite the incident being termed a "manguicidio" (a play on the words "mango" and "magnicidio," meaning "assassination of a powerful leader") by Maduro's critics, Olivo clarified that she had no malicious intentions and was merely hoping to own a home before she dies, a dream that is about to come true.

Argentine soccer star Carlos Tevez, who currently plays for Juventus in Serie A and previously played in the Premier League, believes it is harder to score goals in the Italian league compared to the Premier League. Tevez, who has scored 36 goals in Serie A since joining Juventus in 2013, criticized the midfields in the Premier League as non-existent and suggested that defending is better in Italy. After missing Juventus' match against Parma, Tevez stated that his task of scoring goals had become much more difficult. The former Manchester United and City striker also believes that his current Juventus team is more rounded than the one he played on in 2008, which won the Champions League, and believes they can repeat that success.

In the Premier League match between Crystal Palace and Manchester City, Yaya Toure was accused by Jamie Carragher of neglecting his duties in a five-man wall during a free-kick situation. Carragher criticized Toure for not being enthusiastic, as he seemed to duck contrasting Fernandinho and Vincent Kompany who were active in an attempt to block Jason Puncheon's free-kick, which ultimately proved decisive in the game and highlighted City's nine-point gap behind leaders Chelsea.

An Australian man, aged 50, died suddenly on Wednesday at the 101 Legian Hotel in Kuta, Bali, after collapsing and appearing to suffer a heart attack. The man, who is believed to be from Seymour, Victoria, had been holidaying with a friend at the hotel and was due to stay until April 29. Kuta, known for its long sandy beach and popular with Australian tourists, is a major tourist destination. An autopsy is pending to determine the exact cause of death.

Richie Benaud, a former Australia cricket captain and commentator, passed away last week at the age of 84 due to skin cancer complications. A private funeral service was held in Sydney on Wednesday attended by close family and friends, including ex-players Shane Warne and Ian Chappell. The Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott offered a state funeral, which Daphne Benaud declined, regarding it as a sign of respect for the impact Benaud had on millions nationally and internationally. Benaud, considered one of the most influential characters in cricket during the last century, spent 17 years in the commentating booth after retiring from cricket, for which he is equally renowned for his distinctive voice and style. Tributes poured in from cricket communities worldwide.

A 16-year-old girl named Isobel Attwood has been missing for two days, and friends believe she is in Southampton with a man in his 20s. Isobel attempted to reassure her family through a Facebook post stating that she was safe but needed to get away. Police are concerned for her welfare and are asking for the public's help in finding her, as they believe she could still be in the Winchester or Southampton area.

Manchester City players face significant salary losses if they fail to qualify for the Champions League, with stars such as Sergio Aguero and Yaya Toure at risk of missing out on £500,000 bonuses. City's potential exclusion is due to financial fairplay regulations, and the team is currently placed fourth in the Premier League, four points ahead of Liverpool. Manager Manuel Pellegrini, who has criticized the team's performance in 2015, is facing pressure to secure a top-four finish to ensure Champions League qualification. In the meantime, teams like Manchester United and their manager Louis van Gaal are eying potential transfers, including Juventus midfielder Paul Pogba.

Martin Skrtel, a defender for Liverpool, has denied rumors suggesting he would leave the club this summer, despite links to Wolfsburg and Napoli. Skrtel, who has been with Liverpool since 2008 and has made over 200 league appearances, is expected to renew his contract with the club. His agent also confirmed that there is currently no offer on the table from Wolfsburg, contradicting reports of their interest.

A Texas-based CEO, Cheryl Rios, has faced criticism for stating on Facebook that a woman cannot be president due to her hormones and the potential to start a war. Rios, who supports equal rights, claimed her stance was underpinned by biblical reasoning without specifying a verse. The backlash included accusations of misogyny and hypocrisy on social media, with some questioning her understanding of female leadership in history. Rios responded by asserting her right to her beliefs and stating that women are capable of becoming great lawyers, doctors, and businessowners, but not the president of the country due to the nature of the role. She later clarified that hercomments were not meant to advocate woman abuse or belittle women's intelligence.

1. Atletico Madrid striker Mario Mandzukic, who was physically assaulted during the Champions League quarter-final first leg against Real Madrid, is expected to recover in time for the return leg at Bernabeu on Wednesday.
2. Mandzukic suffered injuries, including a cut to the nose from an elbow by Sergio Ramos and a punch to the stomach from Dani Carvajal, during the first leg that ended 0-0.
3. Despite the injuries, Atletico coach Diego Simeone indicated that Mandzukic, who has been in good form in La Liga, would be favored to play in attack alongside Antoine Griezmann, who scored both goals in the team's 2-1 win over Deportivo in their last La Liga match.

1. Jose Mourinho, the Chelsea manager, incorrectly believed Manchester United's Marouane Fellaini would play in a match against Chelsea, as he had spent the week preparing his team to counter Fellaini's threat.
2. Mourinho was informed by a hotel doorman that Fellaini was not playing, as it was his twin brother Mansour who was disguised as Fellaini at the hotel to get tickets from Eden Hazard.
3. Despite the confusion, Fellaini did play in the match at Stamford Bridge, and Chelsea's Kurt Zouma was tasked with man-marking Fellaini and managed to neutralize his influence in the game.

Dawn Milosky, a 45-year-old resident of Beachwood, New Jersey, was rescued from an overturned and burning 2006 Toyota Solara convertible in Kinnelon, New Jersey, following a police response to a report of erratic driving. Milosky was found unconscious, and officers had to extricate her from the vehicle in just two minutes. Thirty seconds later, the vehicle caught fire. Milosky was charged with DWI, open container, reckless driving, and failure to stay in the right lane. She has reportedly recovered and was airlifted to Morristown Medical Center.

A farmer in China is currently caring for a baby goat with six legs, which has been nicknamed the 'spider goat' and has gained national attention. The goat, which was born 20 days ago and weighs approximately 5kg, is growing healthy and has an 'extraordinary appetite.' Although two of the goat's forelegs have become shorter and no longer touch the ground, it remains playful and is one of the most energetic animals on the farm. The farmer, Xiao Qibin, plans to let the goat grow naturally without seeking medical intervention to remove the extra legs.

1. West Ham United is planning to sign Javier Hernandez, currently on loan from Manchester United at Real Madrid, as part of their summer recruitment, following his recent heroics in the Champions League.

2. Javier Hernandez, who has one year left on his contract at Manchester United, has started only sporadically for Real Madrid this season and is not in the plans of coach Louis van Gaal.

3. West Ham are also pursuing other young transfer targets ahead of their final season at Upton Park, including Sampdoria's Pedro Obiang, FC Sion's Moussa Konate, and Basle's Fabian Schar.

1. Stuart McCall, the interim manager of Scottish Championship club Rangers, has ruled out any discussions about his future before the end of the season, despite restoring a positive atmosphere and securing three straight wins.
2. The former Motherwell boss, who signed until the end of the season with the aim of rekindling Rangers' promotion push, emphasized the team has yet to achieve anything significant in their campaign.
3. Eventual loan signing, Shane Ferguson from Newcastle United, is set to join Rangers next week, but McCall is wary of his immediate game readiness due to a long-term knee injury.

Werder Bremen secured a 1-0 victory over Hamburg SV with a late Franco Di Santo penalty, keeping them in contention for a Europa League spot. The game saw Argentine Di Santo, Zlatko Junuzovic, and Valon Behrami (who was sent off) as key players. Hamburg, managed by new coach Bruno Labbadia, remain in last place, while Bremen moved up to seventh. Meanwhile, second-placed VfL Wolfsburg aim to close the gap between them and leaders Bayern Munich, who currently have a 10-point lead. Bayer Leverkusen are third in the table after their impressive 4-0 win over Hanover 96.

A two-year-old boy fell approximately 10 to 12 feet into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after being dangled over the edge by his mother. The toddler suffered minor bumps and bruises in the fall and was taken to the hospital in stable condition. Witnesses report that the child was not attacked by the cheetahs, with some suggesting they were merely scared by the commotion. The zoo is planning to press charges of child endangerment against the family.

A Russian TV channel gave a mature rating to Hillary Clinton's first campaign video due to fears it might violate Russia's anti-gay propaganda law, which restricts discussions of gay rights and relationships near minors. The brief clip containing two men holding hands in Clinton's video likely triggered the rating. The law has been heavily criticized on an international level for promoting discrimination and increasing homophobia in Russia.

Siem de Jong, Newcastle United's midfielder, returned from a collapsed lung by playing 45 minutes for the Under-21 team in a 2-0 defeat, but was replaced at halftime and seems unlikely to play against Tottenham due to his subdued performance. Forward Facundo Ferreyra replaced de Jong at the break and is yet to make his senior debut, while the game's goals came from Alefe Santos and Farrend Rawson for Derby County.

Chef Ally Lees of Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham has created a three-foot diameter omelette containing 12,000 calories and 945g of protein, which is 16 times the recommended daily intake for a man. The omelette, made with 150 eggs, is claimed to be the biggest ever cooked and is recommended for a group of no fewer than five to consume. The dish was prepared as a promotional offering for Easter.

Three Olympic gold medalists, Jessica Ennis-Hill, Mo Farah, and Greg Rutherford, will participate in the Sainsbury's Anniversary Games in London this summer, having won their golds during Super Saturday in 2012. This three-day event includes a two-day Diamond League meeting and the Sainsbury's IPC Athletics Grand Prix Final, with Ennis-Hill returning for her first appearance since giving birth last year. Tickets for the event, anticipated to be one of the season's major athletic events, are now on sale at britishathletics.org.uk.

In a Rio de Janeiro snack bar, customers were unknowingly consuming pastries filled with stray dog meat. police discovered numerous frozen dog carcasses at the establishment, which was owned by a Chinese businessman, Van Ruilonc. The investigation started due to allegations of mistreatment and forced labor of trafficked Chinese workers. In addition to finding a worker imprisoned in a cage, officers also discovered the quarters filled with the remains of dead dogs.

Ebony Dickens, who used the pseudonym Tiffany Milan, was arrested in East Point, Georgia for a Facebook post threatening to shoot every white cop she sees. The post, which was made on Monday and removed the next day, stated her intent to potentially kill 15 white police officers. Authorities connected Dickens to the post, obtained a search warrant for her residence, and took her into custody. She was charged with disseminating information related to terrorist acts, and a judge set a $10,000 bond for her, banning her from social media.

PSV Eindhoven won the Dutch Eredivisie championship for the first time in seven years by beating Heerenveen 4-1, securing them 79 points and leaving second-placed Ajax Amsterdam unable to catch up. Striker Luuk de Jong scored two headed goals in the first half, with Memphis Depay adding a third with a stunning free kick. The victory is PSV's 22nd league title, making them second only to Ajax in the Netherlands. Meanwhile, Dordrecht moved closer to relegation following a 3-0 loss to Vitesse Arnhem, while AZ Alkmaar secured a place in the Europa League playoffs with a 3-1 home win over ADO Den Haag.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva allegedly died from internal bleeding due to severe beating by his head teacher, Lalit Verma, at Dwarika Prasad School in Railamau village, India. The teacher is accused of beating Shiva for stealing another student's pencil and eraser. This incident is not unique, as there have been previous instances of Indian teachers using extreme corporal punishment leading to fatalities. For example, a nine-year-old boy in Burdwan, West Bengal, died after being beaten with a stick by his private tutor, and a young boy in Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh, was beaten and thrown out of a window onto a busy road due to unpaid school fees.

A gastrointestinal illness has impacted around 100 passengers and five crew members on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship. Symptoms include vomiting, diarrhea, and other gastrointestinal issues. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) are investigating the cause, with representatives set to meet the ship in San Diego on Monday. This is the third reported outbreak of gastrointestinal illness on the Celebrity Infinity, with previous incidents in 2006 and 2013.

A Boston Terrier named Gizmo has gained internet fame by mastering a unique trick called paw-stand walking, where he walks on his hind legs while planting his front feet on the ground, developed out of uncertainty with new boots. Loren Mathieson, Gizmo's owner, recorded the gravity-defying performance, which includes graceful sidesteps, on camera. The video has been viewed over 80,000 times and elicited smiles from viewers.

New Orleans, known for its lively atmosphere and festivals, has implemented a smoke-free policy in most public places, including bars, casinos, and restaurants, as of the start of Tuesday night. The decision was made to protect waiters, musicians, and other workers from secondhand smoke. However, some bar owners and customers who enjoy smoking have expressed concerns over potential loss of revenue and favorite smoking spots, respectively. Legal challenges to the ban, including a lawsuit filed by Harrah's New Orleans and bar owners, are pending.

1. Manchester United's Josh Harrop scored a brace to lead the team to a 3-1 win against West Ham United in the Under 21 Premier League, putting them four points ahead at the top.
2. The game saw a quick turnaround after West Ham took an early lead, with Reece Oxford scoring their first away goal since September.
3. Adnan Januzaj, captain of Manchester United Under 21, provided additional class to the attack, helping the team overcome a half-time deficit and secure the victory.

1. Brisbane's Anglican Archbishop, Phillip Aspinall, has backed a local Catholic priest's appeal to abolish Queensland's 'gay panic' homicide defense, which allows murder charges to be reduced to manslaughter if the defendant claims their victim made a sexual advance.

2. In a statement after an Easter Sunday mass, Aspinall expressed that he finds this defense unreasonable and supports Father Paul Kelly's stance, asserting that violence is never a constructive solution.

3. Beyond his view on the contested legal defense, Aspinall also discouraged violence at anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism in Melbourne, urging followers to resist reacting out of fear and to honor the spirit of resurrection in everyday life.

People magazine has named Sandra Bullock as the world's most beautiful woman of 2015 at the age of 50. In the accompanying interview, Bullock humorously dismissed the title, emphasizing the importance of being a good person and good parent over physical appearance. The cover story also discusses Bullock's home life with her son Louis, her efforts to stay healthy, and her perspective on aging, noting her appreciation for remaining happy and strong. Some observersinterpret the selection of Bullock, the oldest woman to receive the title in the history of the list, as a testament to beauty having no age limit, as seen in the comments from fans on People's Facebook page. Other individuals making the "most beautiful" list in 2015 include Gabrielle Union, Ariana Grande, and Laverne Cox.

An improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, Somalia, on Monday morning, killing six people, including four UNICEF aid workers. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamad condemned the attack as an attack on the future of Somalia. Al-Shabaab, a terrorist group based in Somalia, claimed responsibility for the attack. A separate incident on Sunday resulted in the death of three African Union troops in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia.

A 45-year-old wildlife park owner, Gary Saurage, was called to remove a large, aggressive 400lb, 11ft-long alligator from a family's backyard pond in Beaumont, Texas. In the capture video, Saurage is seen approaching the creature with his bare hands, looking directly into its eyes. The alligator was safely removed and later confirmed as a male, aged around 35-40 years old. This wasn't Saurage's biggest capture; he is currently housing a 12ft 6in alligator named Kong at his wildlife park. Saurage encourages people not to fear alligators as long as they maintain a safe distance and refrain from feeding them.

On Saturday, five militants from the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) were killed and one was wounded in clashes with Turkish military forces in Agri, eastern Turkey. Four Turkish soldiers were also wounded. The fighting involved PKK militants attacking Turkish soldiers who were securing an area ahead of a spring festival. Turkish Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the violence, with Davutoglu attributing it to the PKK's attempt to interrupt the peace process in Turkey, and Erdogan describing it as an attempt at interference. Recently, Ocalan, the longtime leader of the PKK, had urged his followers from prison to lay down their arms and join a "congress" to focus on the future. The conflict between Turkey's Kurdish minority and the Turkish state has been ongoing for over three decades, resulting in an estimated 40,000 deaths.

In Arizona on Friday, tragic incidents occurred when twin 18-month-old boys sadly lost their lives after accidentally falling into a canal. The event took place around 9.45am in the city of Yuma and was believed to be an accident. Following a thorough search, lasting over an hour, the siblings were found in the water. Emergency responders transported them to a local hospital, but they were officially pronounced dead. Investigations are ongoing, with no suspicion of foul play detected. The area where the incident took place is commonly used by families, joggers, and walkers.

Orlando City, coached by Adrian Heath, has expressed interest in signing Manchester United's Javier Hernandez, a move that would likely be commercially beneficial due to Orlando's significant Latin-American fanbase. Hernandez, who has struggled at Real Madrid this season, would be a popular addition to Orlando City's roster, but eight European clubs, including Southampton, Stoke, West Ham, Everton, and several Italian and German teams, are also reportedly interested in signing him. Additionally, Manchester United have reportedly made a revised contract offer to 19-year-old midfielder Andreas Pereira, who has received interest from several European clubs if he does not agree to terms with United.

Joel Burger, age 24, proposed to his long-time girlfriend Ashley King, who accepted. Being childhood friends from New Berlin, Illinois, they plan to creatively integrate the Burger King brand into their wedding, such as serving drinks in personalized Burger King cups, inspired by their nickname ("Burger King") given to them when they were in fifth grade. Despite five years together, their friends continue to tease them about their unique name combination.

A previously unnamed hit band from the 1960s is linked to a notorious pedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London, as revealed in a 1964 police intelligence report. The brothel was also frequented by Jimmy Savile, a star from the Top of the Pops TV show, in the 1970s. However, it's uncertain if the band and Savile attended the brothel at the same time. Detective Superintendent David Grey, who leads Operation Yewtree, began investigating the brothel in 2013 after it was mentioned in another police report. Despite the shared presence at the brothel, Grey indicated that the connection between the band and Savile does not necessarily warrant further investigation without hindsight.

A German Shepherd named Sadie has gained online attention for her unusual and entertaining piano performance at home in Alberta, Canada. She uses her paws to play a minimalist piece on the electric keyboard after turning it on with her nose. Her rendition, lasting approximately 20 seconds, displayed her musical inclinations, as seen in various amusing and adorable reactions captured on video. The six-year-old dog was adopted from an animal rescue shelter in 2009 and reportedly enjoys learning new tricks, with piano playing being the latest addition to her repertoire.

A shoplifting suspect, Ivan Balashov, was caught after taking a selfie with a smartphone he intended to steal, but found less desirable. The police identified him when they found the selfie on the stolen phone left behind at the store, leading to his arrest. He was later found guilty and received a three-month suspended sentence.

The first trailer for the documentary "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name" was released, offering a look into late British singer Amy Winehouse's life and career. Winehouse discusses her artistic journey, expressing ambivalence about fame and her belief that she would not be able to handle it. The film, set for UK release on July 3, integrates extensive unseen archive footage and previously unheard tracks, and has been endorsed by Winehouse's family after gaining support from the team behind the award-winning documentary "Senna." A U.S. release date for the film has yet to be announced.

This week ("The Big Bang Theory" on Thursday 8 p.m. ET, CBS), two renowned actresses return to the show, potentially making it one of the best episodes this season. On Saturday May 2 at 11:30 p.m. on NBC, Scarlett Johansson hosts "Saturday Night Live" following the release of her new "Avengers" movie. In the dramedy "Mom" (Thursday 9:30 p.m., CBS), Allison Janney continues to deliver Emmy-worthy performances. The season finale airs this week. "Backstrom" (Thursday 9 p.m., Fox) has yet to be renewed for another season, but fans should not miss the season finale of the Rainn Wilson crime drama. "Blue Bloods" (Friday 10 p.m., CBS) concludes its two-part season finale with uncertainty over its future. 1. Fans of Downton Abbey can look forward to the potential return of Violet, Countess of Grantham, as played by Dame Maggie Smith, in a new US show The Gilded Age from the creator of Downton Abbey, Julian Fellowes.

2. Set in late 19th Century New York, The Gilded Age will show an earlier version of Violet and other characters from Downton Abbey, including Robert, Earl of Grantham, and his wife Cora (American-born in Downton Abbey), as they take on the high society families of New York, including the Vanderbilt, Astor, and Rockefeller families.

3. Filmed by NBC, The Gilded Age focuses on "robber barons" and industrialists accumulating wealth during the late 19th Century, and it is expected to go on air as early as September, while the sixth and final series of Downton Abbey is set to air later this year on ITV.

Steven Gerrard, who is set to depart Liverpool at the end of the season for LA Galaxy, has been selected to start the FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley. He returns to the squad after a three-match ban, and manager Brendan Rodgers described him as a "special player" who is "definitely ready" for the game. Gerrard, a key player for Liverpool, has experienced FA Cup glory before, with his first triumph coming in 2001 against Arsenal.

A new, original Dr. Seuss book titled "What Pet Should I Get?" is set to debut on July 28, featuring the spirited brother and sister from "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish." The book's pre-orders have surpassed expectations, leading to an increased first printing of 1 million copies. The manuscript and illustrations for the new volume were found in the Geisel family's California home after Theodor Geisel's death in 1991 and have been set aside for publication since their rediscovery in 2013.

Jessica Carey, driving three hours to see her grandmother, surprised her with a tattoo of a childhood portrait of her grandmother Patty Lawing. The tattoo, done by husband Aaron Carey, depicts a young Patty with long red hair, wearing a smart blouse and jacket. The emotional reaction, captured on film, showed Patty unable to hold back tears, shaking, and waving her arms. The video, recorded in February, has recently surfaced online. Jessica shared the footage, stating that her grandmother is one of her favorites and that she wanted to immortalize her in this unique way.

Annegret Raunigk, a 65-year-old mother-of-13 from Berlin, is set to make medical history by giving birth to quadruplets in the coming weeks, making her the oldest woman worldwide to have quadruplets. Having undergone fertility treatment involving donated sperm and eggs, Raunigk, a primary school teacher, claims she feels fit and doesn't expect any complications during the delivery. Known for her previous pregnancy at age 55, Raunigk has 13 children from five different fathers, with her oldest child being 44 years old. Despite the high risk associated with quadruplet pregnancies in her age group, her physician, Dr. Kai Hertwig, has reported that her pregnancy is proceeding as expected.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, has announced plans to launch an unmanned rover aboard an Epsilon rocket to the moon by 2018, intend to explore the lunar surface and develop new soft-landing technology. The mission, if approved, will likely cost between $83.4 million and $125 million. JAXA aims to improve upon previous successes, including the SELENE craft sent to the moon in 2008, and catch up to neighboring countries such as China and India, which have already executed significant extraterrestrial missions.

1. The outbreak of dengue fever has impacted several top Brazilian football teams, with Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero, Palmeiras reserve goalkeeper Aranha, and Santos striker Leo Cittadini being among the affected players.
2. Players have resorted to using insect repellent during practice sessions and clubs have sought assistance from health officials to inspect training centers for mosquito breeding sites.
3. The prevalence of dengue fever has significantly increased across Brazil in 2015, with more than 460,000 cases reported so far, accounting for almost 5,000 cases per day and resulting in over 130 fatalities according to the health ministry.

James Wilson, Manchester United striker, has expressed a desire to incorporate aspects of his teammates' styles into his own game. Specifically, he would like to replicate Wayne Rooney's free-kick ability, Robin van Persie's movement, and Radamel Falcao's instincts in the 18-yard box. Wilson has made 16 appearances for Manchester United this season, scoring once in the Premier League.

A triple tragedy occurred in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, where Archie Brown Jr., a father-of-four, was struck and killed after hitting a 2-year-old who ran into the street. At the scene, an unidentified gunman shot and killed Brown Jr. and a 15-year-old, though it is unclear what the 15-year-old's connection to the incident was. Police believe the shootings may have been in revenge for the 2-year-old's death, as suggested by a local alderman. The perpetrator is still at large, and authorities have released few details about the tragic incident.

The article presents a minor boy from Memphis, Tennessee, who has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers for posting pictures and videos depicting gang-related activities, including guns, drugs, and references to violence. His material has sparked criticism from the community and other Twitter users who view it as disturbing and damaging. The boy, in response, has defended his actions, stating that he has faced a challenging year and his critics are causing stress to his mother. Additionally, the article highlights the growing concern among authorities regarding the use of social media, such as Twitter, to promote and perpetuate gang culture in the United States.

1. Former Redgum frontman John Schumann has expressed disappointment over the use of his song "I Was Only 19" at anti-Islam rallies organized by Reclaim Australia, as the song was written to promote compassion, tolerance, and inclusiveness.
2. The song, which is an anthem about the plight of Vietnam veterans, was played at one of the rallies, where an anti-racism group clashed with supporters of Reclaim Australia, resulting in violence, arrests, and minor injuries.
3. Federal Opposition Leader Bill Shorten has condemned the violence, stating that there is no place for such behavior in any protests or expressions of freedom of speech. He also argued against the claim that Muslims are planning to bring Sharia law to Australia, comparing it to previous unfounded fears about Irish Catholics.

Rutland's previous career in the City of London ended in disgrace in 2012, when he was banned from trading due to market abuse, and he later sustained facial injuries from a mugging.

Jia Binhui, a 25-year-old leukemia patient from Yunlong County in Yunnan Province, China, is hopeful that a self-made alternative treatment using a wooden structure over hot coals can effectively fight his cancer since he cannot afford hospital treatment. This method, inspired by advice from unspecified experts, involves lying on a makeshift contraption above a fire, allegedly reaching temperatures above 42 degrees Celsius, which could potentially kill the cancerous cells. Despite his dire financial situation and the experimental nature of this treatment, Jia remains determined and continues to use the homemade device, sharing updates on his Weibo account.

Queens Park Rangers are planning to bring Leroy Fer back from a knee injury to boost their relegation fight efforts. Fer was injured in February and has struggled with both form and fitness since joining from Norwich in the summer. Manager Chris Ramsey hopes to have Fer in the squad for the London derby against West Ham, acknowledging that they are taking a risk due to his ongoing recovery and recurring injury concerns. Other players like Richard Dunne and Yun Suk-Young are also returning to fitness, but notable absences include Rio Ferdinand.

Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas from Team Sky avoided a major crash in the final kilometer of Scheldeprijs, but teammate Elia Viviani was unfortunately involved in the incident. Viviani was vying for position ahead of the expected sprint finish and sustained injuries to his arm and ribs, requiring x-rays. Katusha's Alexander Kristoff won the race, with only 14 riders contesting the sprint, while the rest of Team Sky, including Wiggins and Thomas, remain in good shape for Paris-Roubaix on Sunday.

Aston Villa players received messages of encouragement from fans, displaying them in their dressing room before the FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool. Jack Grealish, a 19-year-old player, appreciated the support on Twitter while also sharing a picture of Wembley Stadium. The message from Mike Shenaniganz Cope, a supporter, read: "You have to put up with the rain to see the rainbow! Three seasons of rain boys, time to find the end of that rainbow and prove we're the pride of the Midlands!" Both Grealish and goalkeeper Brad Guzan shared the contents of their messages with the team, with one instructing them to "fight like Lions." Grealish warmed up alongside Fabian Delph and Scott Sinclair before the match.

A 12-year-old named Hanghang in central China was seriously injured when his old, exploding phone caused deep injuries, exposing part of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. ThePhone exploded while he was using it to alarm clock while getting ready for school. Experts believe the most common cause of phone explosions is improper charging, such as leaving the phone on the charger or using it while charging, which can lead to overheating and an explosion. Hanghang is currently in the hospital and is expected to undergo several operations to repair the damage.

Mike Rowe, the host of "Somebody's Gotta Do It," met Chad Pregracke, founder of Living Lands & Waters, a nonprofit dedicated to cleaning U.S. waterways. Pregracke, awarded CNN Hero of the Year in 2013, has cleaned over 8.4 million pounds of trash from rivers, and his mission for 2015 is to remove an additional 500,000 pounds. Rowe was given a tour of Pregracke's 150-foot solar-powered barge, a mobile home, office, and dumpster made from a recycled strip club, used as living quarters during clean-up projects. For those interested in contributing, visit LivingLandsAndWaters.org/Get-Involved/ to learn how to help.

The eerie, abandoned 11th-century town of Balestrino, located in Tuscany, Italy, was filmed using a drone. The video showcases the crumbling buildings, including a picturesque castle on a hill, and the landscape's haunting silence. The town's former 800 inhabitants, who once resided there, fled due to seismic instability over 60 years ago, with an 1887 earthquake measuring 6.7 on the Richter scale causing significant damage. Today, Balestrino is known for its ghostly atmosphere and is often considered haunted in local folklore.

1. At an event in Anaheim, director J.J. Abrams and the "Star Wars: Episode VII - The Force Awakens" cast unveiled the movie's trailer, received an overwhelmingly positive response, and highlighted key elements such as Han Solo's return, a new planet setting, and characters Poe, Rey, and Finn.
2. Abrams revealed that the new film will feature less CGI than the prequels, emphasizing practical sets, and confirmed that the soccer-ball-like droid BB-8 is not computer-generated.
3. The panel also showcased other new features like a "Star Wars"-themed 787 Dreamliner, Stormtroopers, and Leia's altered wardrobe, with no metal bikini in sight. The movie is set for release on December 18.

Former Toronto Mayor Rob Ford has announced that he will undergo an eight-to-ten-hour surgery to remove a cancerous tumor in his abdomen on May 11. The procedure comes after he completed five rounds of chemotherapy and nearly a month of radiation, which has shrunk the tumor significantly. Ford hopes to return to work as a city councilor in September and expressed gratitude to his medical staff, family, and the people of Toronto for their support.

A South African university, the University of Cape Town, has successfully removed the statue of British colonialist Cecil Rhodes following a month-long student-led campaign using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall. The students argue that Rhodes represents a racist legacy and does not align with the ideals they promote. Some critics, such as singer Steve Hofmeyr, view the removal as erasing history and advocate for more monuments rather than fewer. With the removal of the statue, students celebrate but also indicate that their movement is not finished yet.

Michael Phelps, the 18-time Olympic gold-medalist, made a winning return to competitive swimming in Arizona after a six-month suspension for a drink-driving conviction. He won the 100 meters butterfly race with a time of 52.38 seconds, beating Ryan Lochte. Despite missing this summer's World Championships in Kazan, Russia, Phelps aims to compete in the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro.

A New York woman died by suicide on Sunday, hanging from a third-floor fire escape in Crown Heights. Witnesses reported seeing her body for over an hour, some initially mistaking it for a Halloween prank. The woman's identity is yet to be released while authorities notify her family, and neighbors describe her as a friendly, sociable individual with known mental health issues. The incident has left witnesses traumatized, and resources for those struggling with mental health are available at the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline.

1. In a thrilling Rhone Valley derby match, Lyon and Saint-Etienne ended in a 2-2 draw, with Clinton N'Jie, Romain Hamouma, and Christophe Jallet scoring for their respective sides. Lyon's draw propels them to the top of Ligue 1 on equal points with reigning champions Paris St Germain.

2. Lille secured a 2-0 victory over Bordeaux at the Stade Pierre Mauroy, with Nolan Roux and Adama Traore on the scoresheet. This win keeps Lille within sight of fourth place, as they are now four points behind Bordeaux but have a game in hand.

3. Montpellier earned a narrow 1-0 victory over Caen, with Brazilian defender Hilton scoring early in the game. This result sees Montpellier move up to seventh in the Ligue 1 standings, while Caen remain in 13th position after a poor run of six league matches.

1. Arsene Wenger was surprised by the significant contributions of Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin in Arsenal's late push for the Premier League title. He originally did not expect these players to play pivotal roles due to their previous performances and loan statuses.

2. Bellerin, a 20-year-old Spanish full-back, scored the opening goal in an impressive 4-1 win against Liverpool, with his performance being a major factor in controlling Raheem Sterling. Wenger praised Bellerin's pace, low center of gravity, and defending ability during one-on-one situations, stating that he has mental quality evidenced by his goal in a big game.

3. Manager Arsene Wenger had all but written off Francis Coquelin, sending him on loan to Charlton before Christmas, but the defensive midfielder has since become a vital part of Arsenal's success, showing promising defensive skills and maturity. Bellerin's performance earned him praise from teammates Nacho Monreal and Oliver Giroud. However, Wenger conceded that Bellerin was lucky not to be sent off for a mistimed

A two-hour remake of the cult classic film "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" is in development by Fox, with Kenneth Ortega serving as director, executive producer, and choreographer. This project, titled "The Rocky Horror Picture Show Event", is being produced by Fox 21 Television Studios and The Jackal Group, and it's intended to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the original film. The special is still casting-contingent, and it will be filmed in advance, but the specific air date is yet to be announced. This isn't the first attempt to adapt the film for television; a 2002 adaptation timed to the 30th anniversary never materialized. FOX also has a live musical production of "Grease" scheduled for January 2016, and NBC recently announced plans for a live version of "The Wiz".

AS Roma has been ordered to partially close their stadium for their next home game due to offensive banners displayed during a recent match against Napoli. The banners, directed towards the mother of a Napoli fan who was killed in violent clashes last year, were deemed provocative and insulting. Roma won the match, but the club and their fans have faced punishment for the incident. The taunts, aimed at Antonella Leardi, have been widely condemned, with Roma's president expressing his disapproval, calling for an end to such behavior to prevent renewal of such pain.

Ellen White, a Notts County player, experienced a significant career moment by scoring a stunning free kick against her former club Arsenal in the Women's Super League. The goal was a result of a unique setup at training grounds, during which Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood initially caused confusion but ultimately played a role in the score. Despite the thrilling goal, White missed a subsequent penalty that could have made it 2-0. Arsenal salvaged a late equalizer through Chioma Ubogagu's debut goal, ensuring a 1-1 draw.

Arsene Wenger acknowledges discussions with Eden Hazard's agent in 2012, but opted against signing him as Arsenal couldn't match Chelsea's financial offer of £32million. The decision could prove regrettable given Hazard's exceptional season at Chelsea, where he is currently in contention for Player of the Year. Wenger believes Alexis Sanchez, his counterpart at Arsenal, will also be a strong contender for the award due to his impressive debut season.

Stephen Akers-Belcher, the former Mayor of Hartlepool, was dismissed from his care manager role at Newcastle City Council due to gross misconduct. This was a result of him taking time off work to attend a funeral, but evidence showed he had attended an official function on HMS Warrior instead, which was 323 miles away. Akers-Belcher claims the dismissal was in response to whistleblowing allegations, but the council denies this. The council maintains that Akers-Belcher had failed to provide evidence for his absence and that his allegations were investigated without finding further action necessary.

A senior doctor, Dr. John Parker, who had been working at an Australian-run Ebola treatment clinic in Sierra Leone, was taken to Westmead Hospital in Sydney after developing flu-like symptoms. Tests performed at the hospital have confirmed that he does not have Ebola, and no further testing is required. His employer, Aspen Medical, confirmed that he followed protocol by notifying authorities as a precaution. Over 10,000 deaths have been reported from the deadly Ebola virus in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

A nine-year-old boy, Frankie Franz, emulated Barcelona star Martin Montoya's impressive 27-yard, basketball-hoop goal and managed to score it twice in his garden. This was inspired by watching a viral video of Montoya's goal recorded at Barcelona's Ciutat Esportiva training ground. Frankie, an academy player with Dagenham and Redbridge Football Club, showed remarkable skill and confidence in duplicating the feat on his first attempt. His mother, Lucy, described the impressive display as "very special." Despite not being on camera, Lucy mentioned that Frankie successfully netted again immediately after his first attempt. Frankie aspires to play for Real Madrid or Barcelona in the future.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 features a diverse collection of cricket images from around the globe, with the winning shot depicting Dwayne Bravo taking an exceptional catch for the West Indies against Australia during the ICC World Twenty20 competition. The competition also includes compelling images of amateur players, such as children playing on a rubbish tip in Bangladesh and a club player in Kent. Other noteworthy entries feature incidents like a broken nose for England bowler Stuart Broad, a stumps-shattering delivery from Dale Steyn to Bangladesh A's Nurul Hasan, and a victorious celebration by Sri Lanka, among others.

1. A New Jersey judge dismissed a father's claim that his ex-wife abused her parental discretion by taking their 11-year-old daughter to a Pink concert in 2013, finding that the mother did not exceed the boundaries of reasonable parental judgment.
2. The judge's decision, which included a discussion of the history of rock 'n' roll and the role of judges as referees in custody battles, ruled that while Pink's performances can be suggestive, they are not necessarily inappropriate for preteens.
3. The judge found that the mother and daughter had a positive experience at the concert, and the decision ended with the judge quoting lyrics from Pink's songs as examples of messages for adolescents.

1. The coastal town of Salcombe in Devon, known as 'Chelsea-on-Sea', has surpassed London as the most expensive place to buy property in the UK, with an average property price of £671,759, according to new data.
2. While the average cost of property in some of the UK's most expensive cities like Oxford, Bath, and Edinburgh is considerably lower, the average value of a waterfront property in Salcombe even tops some of London's priciest postcodes, including Notting Hill and Regent's Park.
3. With a yearly increase of 10% in property prices and a million-pound view, Salcombe continues to attract UK travelers looking for a luxury getaway, offering waterfront rooms at the Salcombe Harbour Hotel & Spa for £425 during the summer season.

Celtic football club has expressed disappointment over ticket prices for their upcoming Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness Caledonian Thistle at Hampden. They believe the prices, set at £23 for North and South stands, £15 for adults and £5 for concessions in the East Stand, are too high. Celtic has requested that the SFA review and lower North Stand ticket prices. The SFA has responded, stating that ticket prices have been unchanged for the past four years, and all four participating clubs were consulted on pricing. The SFA also mentioned that revenues from gate, broadcast, and advertising are aggregated and distributed evenly to the competing teams. Meanwhile, Celtic manager Ronny Deila prepares his team for their upcoming SPL clash with St Mirren.

A 16-year-old student, Rebecca Rice, was allowed to bring her 11-year-old Labrador, Holly, into a GCSE French exam to help alleviate her nerves. Rebecca had tried various methods to calm down but found that only her dog could comfort her. After consulting with teacher Lorette Esteve, it was decided that Holly could accompany Rebecca during the five-minute recorded French oral test. The strategy was successful, as Rebecca felt more relaxed with her dog by her side. Staff at Bodmin College in Cornwall have implemented measures to reduce stress during the exam period, such as allowing drinks, a lucky key ring, or a friend in the room.

Anders Lindegaard, the Manchester United goalkeeper, enjoyed a day off with his wife Misse Beqiri, a Swedish model, whom he married last year in Mauritius. Despite struggling for playing time at United, Lindegaard frequently shares photos of his family on Instagram. Misse Beqiri, who has a large Instagram following, is a well-known model with Albanian roots. Despite limited minutes at Old Trafford, Lindegaard has been linked with a move away from the club but has had little success finding a new team.

Manchester United goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes, following a recent derby win against Manchester City, took a day off to visit a theme park, basking in the English sun. The Red Devils have experienced a tumultuous season, struggling initially to secure a top-four finish but gaining momentum to challenge Arsenal for second place. The future of both De Gea and Valdes remains uncertain, with Valdes facing limited game time at Old Trafford since his free transfer to the club.

A 75-year-old piano teacher, John Goodwin, shot himself outside the Rockingham County Superior Courthouse in New Hampshire on Friday, while jurors were deliberating on charges of aggravated felonious sexual assault against an underage student. Goodwin, who pleaded not guilty, was awaiting a jury's verdict in a trial that began this week. His condition following the self-inflicted gunshot wound is currently unknown. The New Hampshire Attorney General's Office is expected to release further details about the incident later in the day.

Amazon removed a mobile game called "Rescue the Anorexia Girl" due to public outrage over its controversial content. The game, which was marketed on Amazon and Android platforms, invited players to throw food at a cartoon girl battling anorexia. The game's objective was to save the girl before she disappeared, and if missed, she would lose weight and eventually die. Critics, including mental health advocates, argued the game further stigmatized those suffering from eating disorders.

Researchers are working to replicate the cognitive abilities of honeybees to power drones, with the aim of creating a robot that thinks, senses, and acts like them. The Green Brain Project, a collaboration between the Universities of Sheffield and Sussex, is leading this effort by building an artificial brain based on the honeybee's brain, using circuits that mimic the organic brain's function. Initial tests have included a drone flying down a corridor, and the team is currently focusing on navigation, flight tests with the BeeBot quadcopter, and testing with chemosensors.

A newly-wed Air Malta crew, a pilot and a cabin crew member, took their guests on a romantic flyover in the shape of two giant hearts over the Mediterranean to celebrate their wedding. The Airbus A319 aircraft traceable via flightradar24.com flew two circuits around Malta, skirting the Italian coast, before the status 'Just Married' appeared on the MIA's arrivals board. Some spectators on social media saw it as a creative training flight, while others interpreted it as a romantic PR stunt or a marriage proposal.

In the Kristiansand Zoo, Melvin the giraffe, a popular attraction, died unprovoked when an eland antelope, the second largest antelope species, gored him near his lungs and heart. This tragic event occurred when Melvin had accidently gotten his head stuck in the enclosure's fence. Approximately 30 people, including young families and children, bore witness to the traumatic scene. Zoo officials remain perplexed as to the reason behind the antelope's attack on the young giraffe.

A restaurant in Leuven, Belgium, charged a mother 36p to heat up her baby's feeding bottle, sparking outrage on Twitter and earning the restaurant manager the title of 'stingiest boss in Europe.' The mother had gone to the Rubens eatery with her family and was shocked to find a charge for the bottle-warming service on her bill, which totaled around £20. The restaurant chain later explained that such a charge would only occur if customers are explicitly informed that the service is paid.

North Korea's cargo ship, the Mu Du Bong, was detained by Mexico in July after running aground. Mexico defended their actions due to the ship's owner, North Korea's Ocean Maritime Management company, being blacklisted by the UN Security Council for evading sanctions. Mexico's U.N. mission stated that the 33 North Korean crew members are free, staying at a hotel, and will soon be returned to North Korea. This situation contrasts with the case of the Chong Chon Gang in 2013, where Panama found undeclared weaponry on the ship and held the crew and vessel for months, eventually releasing it after North Korea paid a fine.

Prime Minister David Cameron will announce an additional 600,000 childcare spaces at a cost of £350 million to help offset increasing childcare expenses. The measure is aimed at reducing the barrier to employment due to high childcare costs, particularly for second earners. The Conservatives plan to fund this initiative by decreasing tax relief on pension contributions for individuals earning over £150,000.

Manchester City's young squad reinforced their 3-0 first-leg lead against Leicester City with two late goals from Isaac Buckley and Brandon Barker, securing a Youth Cup final spot. Layton Ndukwu provided Leicester hope with a penalty, but City's response was swift, with Buckley and later Barker scoring to extend their lead. City will face Chelsea in the final, with the first leg scheduled for April 20 at the City Football Academy Stadium and the second leg a week later at Stamford Bridge.

Russian President Vladimir Putin, during his annual Q&A session, dismissed Western sanctions as an attempt to limit Russia's development, not just relating to Ukraine and Crimea. He defended the sale of a sophisticated air defense system to Iran, stating it would not pose a threat to Israel, but rather be a defense weapon. The event, criticized as a mockery of democracy, is a highly produced opportunity for Putin to address the public and the world, with 2.4 million questions submitted this year. Notably, last year, Edward Snowden appeared by video link, addressing Putin on Russia's surveillance practices.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood will evaluate Gary Gardner's ability during pre-season after a successful loan spell at Nottingham Forest. Gardner, who is eager to impress, scored a noteworthy free-kick in front of Sherwood during a game against Watford. Originally a part of Villa's academy, Gardner had previously expressed his interest in playing for Forest again if necessary, and still sees Villa as his main club due to his long association with the team.

In Santiago, Chile, three people were killed and several others injured during a stampede at the Tsunami nightclub, while British punk band Doom was performing. The crowd tried forcing their way into the club, causing a crush outside that led to structural collapse and fatalities. Police have arrested several individuals in connection with the tragic incident, while the dead and critical victims are believed to be in their 20s and 30s. The band Doom, known for their Crust Punk music, played tracks like Anti-Social and Raining Napalm during the event.

Bayern Munich advanced to the semi-finals of the German Cup after a 5-3 penalty shoot-out victory over Bayer Leverkusen, but manager Pep Guardiola expressed concern about their lack of scoring touch in recent games, attributing it to the absence of Franck Ribery and Arjen Robben. Robben is out until May due to a stomach muscle tear, while Ribery is recovering from an ankle injury and his return date is uncertain. Guardiola believes the team lacks players suitable for one-on-one situations with Ribery and Robben missing. The team will face Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga this Saturday, and will need to overcome their attacking difficulties to maintain their lead over Wolfsburg. The only goal scored by Munich in their last three games was by Robert Lewandowski against his former club Borussia Dortmund, and they will meet again in the German Cup semi-final.

Derry Mathews' world title challenge is in doubt due to Richar Abril's withdrawal for the second time, potentially jeopardizing Abril's WBA lightweight belt. Mathews, who recently secured a fifth-round knockout against Gyorgy Mezei Jnr in Liverpool, might still fight for a version of the title on April 18 in his hometown. Discussions are underway between Mathews' promoter, the WBA, and Abril's representatives regarding the title's current status, with Mathews expressing disappointment over Abril's inability to commit to the fight.

1. English Bulldog named Hazel exhibits a puppy's natural curiosity by attempting to interact with a washing basket, resulting in the basket falling and Hazel landing on the floor.
2. In a series of videos uploaded to her YouTube and Instagram channels, Hazel is shown exploring various household items, such as a skateboard, a mirror, and a collar.
3. Known for her adorable antics, Hazel's playful behavior, which includes chewing on the basket's rim, exemplifies her charm and endearing personality.

The six-part BBC drama Wolf Hall, airing in the U.S. for the first time, has been criticized by American Catholic bishops for its "prejudice-laden presentation" and "evidence-flouting caricature" of historical figures, particularly Thomas Cromwell and Thomas More, portrayed as a "monster" and a "sleazy, mean-spirited" character, respectively. The drama's depiction of the Tudor period is criticized for its supposed anti-Catholic bias, while the U.S. media, in general, expects the show to be a compelling import, with Damian Lewis as King Henry VIII and Claire Foy as Anne Boleyn. Some U.S. media, however, have expressed concern over the potential distortion of historical facts and the possible obscuring of important historical lessons in the adaptation of Hilary Mantel's book.

Today, Fort Hood victims, including Staff Sergeant Shawn Manning, are to receive Purple Heart medals, yet there are claims they are being denied crucial financial support. Manning, who was shot six times during the 2009 attack, alleges he has been denied benefits due to the Army rejecting his claims that his injuries were sustained in the line of duty. The Army rejects his injuries as combat-related since the 2015 National Defense Authorization Act does not offer combat benefits for those permanently disabled in attacks inspired or motivated by foreign terrorist organizations. Manning fears other survivors of the shooting rampage will be in a similar position and may miss out on $800 a month in benefits, as well as back pay. It is known that the attack was inspired by al-Qaeda, as Army psychiatrist Major Nidal Hasan, the attacker, had exchanged emails with Anwar al-Awlaki, an al-Qaeda spokesman.

1. Newcastle United head coach John Carver believes he has the hardest job in football due to fan discontent with owner Mike Ashley's management, a losing streak, and a depleted squad.

2. The fans are planning a boycott of the upcoming home match against Tottenham Hotspur in protest against Ashley's running of the club, citing his lack of investment and ambition despite Newcastle's record profits and excess funds.

3. Despite the planned boycott, Carver has urged fans to support the team and has foreseen Derby County's Steve McClaren as his likely successor, with the latter already tipped as a potential replacement should Carver face the Newcastle axe.

Jordan Spieth, a 21-year-old American golfer, has won the 2015 Masters tournament at Augusta, breaking several records including becoming the first to reach 19 under par. He had a four-shot lead going into the final day and maintained it throughout, ending with a final round of 70. Spieth previously finished joint-second at last year's Masters, and his victory follows a series of impressive golf achievements, including becoming the fourth youngest winner in PGA history, winning the PGA Tour Rookie of the Year, and finishing as low amateur at the US Open in 2012. Born in Texas, Spieth gained attention as a teenager and turned professional after his second year at the University of Texas. Off the course, he is in a relationship with high school sweetheart Annie Verret and recently purchased a mansion in his hometown for $2.3 million.

Beatrice Tollman, the founder of a luxury hotel chain, donated £20,000 to the Conservative party in the UK, but her past involvement in tax evasion charges has come to light, which may cause embarrassment for Prime Minister David Cameron. Her husband, Stanley Tollman, had previously pleaded guilty to tax evasion and spent five years fighting extradition. The Conservative party has announced they will return donations from the Tollmans following these revelations.

A marketing coordinator named Poppy Smart reported sexual harassment to police after enduring daily wolf-whistling and sexist comments from builders during her commute in Worcester city center. She felt the wolf-whistling was as distressing as racial discrimination and compared the experience to an awful walking journey. The police treated the incident as a possible case of anti-social behavior and the construction company dealing with the workforce responsible. Despite not being a specific offense, repeated obscene comments from the workmen could potentially lead to a breach of the peace conviction. In 2012, UK Prime Minister David Cameron also declined to criminalize wolf-whistling, arguing that harassment laws already in place sufficiently addressed the issue. However, activists such as Sarah Green of the End Violence Against Women Coalition argue that such behaviors contribute to everyday sexism and should be stamped out. Building firms have also started banning wolf-whistling among their workforce.

A UK teenager named Lily Sharp pranked her own mother by pretending to have been kidnapped, referencing the Liam Neeson film Taken. She convincingly created a narrative where an intruder had entered their home, taken her phone, and demanded a ransom of £4000. Her mother, believing the kidnapper was in possession of her daughter, became increasingly frantic. Lily eventually revealed the prank, but her mother was not amused. The prank received widespread attention on Twitter with over 18,000 retweets and 25,000 favorites.

In the first ODI of a series, Bangladesh defeated Pakistan by 79 runs in Dhaka, with Tamim Iqbal and Mushfiqur Rahim scoring centuries for Bangladesh (329/6) and Pakistan managing 250 in reply. Pakistan lost key wickets early in their innings, while Bangladesh's partnership between Iqbal and Rahim helped them recover from a difficult start. The second ODI is scheduled for Sunday in Mirpur.

Todd Kincannon, a 33-year-old attorney and former South Carolina Republican Party executive director, has been arrested and charged with criminal domestic violence. The arrest warrant alleges that Kincannon grabbed his wife's arm and threatened to kill her, himself, and her family during an incident in March. A bond hearing is scheduled for the following day. Additionally, it was reported that his wife has evidence of verbal abuse and possible domestic abuse from Kincannon, including over forty-eight hours of audio recordings and photographic evidence. Kincannon has gained a reputation on Twitter for sending inflammatory tweets that have been accused of racism and sexism. He had previously refused to apologize for these tweets and appears to have deleted his Twitter account following his recent arrest.

Jordan Spieth, fresh from winning the Masters and breaking Tiger Woods' tournament record, is playing in the RBC Heritage Classic this week despite a busy schedule of media appearances and interviews. He is determined to maintain his chase for world No. 1, currently held by Rory McIlroy. Spieth's success at the previous two RBC Heritage Classics, where he finished 9th in 2013 and 12th last year, has made him confident about this tournament. Several top-ranked players, including defending champion Matt Kuchar, will also be participating in the event.

Samantha Cameron, wife of former British Prime Minister David Cameron, has demonstrated her affinity for the American psychedelic rock band Poliça, which celebrates radical feminist Shulamith Firestone as a muse. The band's music features aggressive and violent imagery, with lyrics that express discontent towards traditional masculine roles and relationships. Their latest album, Shulamith, is named after Firestone, who advocated for a liberated world without families, childbirth, or gender distinctions, and is known for her revolutionary 1970 manifesto, The Dialectic Of Sex. Samantha Cameron was recently spotted at a Poliça gig in Shoreditch, London.

1. The Australian government plans to impose a 10% Goods and Services Tax (GST) on movie and music downloads from streaming services like Netflix and Apple, potentially generating billions of additional revenue, as well as affecting consumers purchasing products online from overseas.

2. The tax could impact companies such as Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and eBay, but consumer advocacy group Choice suggests that the government should focus on reducing domestic costs and improving access to content rather than introducing the tax.

3. Tech-savvy consumers may circumvent the tax by using Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) to conceal their location and appear outside the country. Netflix has agreed to adjust its service cost to comply with any new laws and regulations.

Stephen A. Smith, an ESPN First Take anchor, is facing criticism for suggesting that Floyd Mayweather Jr's boxing career should be judged independently from his domestic violence history. In a discussion about Mayweather's upcoming fight against Manny Pacquiao, Smith implied that Cari Champion's stance against Mayweather was due to her being a woman, igniting controversy. This situation resurfaced memories of Smith's previous controversy in July 2021, where he victim-blamed in reference to the Ray Rice scandal.

A 12-year-old boy named Mahendra Ahirwar from India has a rare condition that causes his head to hang perpetually, restricting his movement and ability to perform daily tasks. His parents, Mukesh and Sumitra Ahirwar, have voiced their despair as medical professionals have been unable to diagnose or treat his condition, leaving them with the harrowing choice of watching him suffer or hoping for a miracle. The community has accusingly blamed Mahendra's disability on Mukesh's past sins, adding to the family's anguish. Despite limited resources, the family continues to seek medical help and remain hopeful that Mahendra can live a normal life.

1. Switzerland ranks as the world's happiest nation, according to a new study on global wellbeing. This is due to factors such as healthy GDP, strong social bonds, and increasing life expectancy.

2. The list of happiest countries is dominated by European nations, particularly Scandinavian ones, with Iceland jumping from number 9 to number 2 due to factors such as beautiful scenery and cultural history.

3. The lowest-ranking countries are those affected by war and extreme poverty, with Syria, Burundi, and Togo at the bottom of the list. The United States is below Canada in the rankings, despite often criticizing its northern neighbor.

The article previews the upcoming Premier League match between Burnley and Arsenal at Turf Moor. Burnley's midfielder Matt Taylor could potentially make his return from a long-term achilles injury, while Ross Wallace and Steven Reid might also be available. However, Dean Marney and Kevin Long remain ruled out. Arsenal's Laurent Koscielny and Wojciech Szczesny face fitness tests ahead of the match. If Koscielny passes, he will play for the Gunners. Jack Wilshere, Mikel Arteta, Abou Diaby, and Mathieu Debuchy are also back in contention for the match. Camellias are versatile, evergreen shrubs known for their contrasting foliage and bright flowers. They thrive in acidic, free-draining, and nutrient-rich soil but dislike alkaline or neutral ground, so they are suitable for containers filled with ericaceous compost. Camellias can be pruned to keep them compact or encourages to grow as hedging, on walls, over arches, or among other shrubs. They are hardy to frost and have a long flowering period that does not require abundant sunlight. Potted camellias tend to lose their charm after five to six years but can be easily propagated through root cuttings, and this is the best time to take such cuttings. The article suggests buying camellias now to enjoy their variety, with popular choices such as the semi-double, subtly veined pink Donation. Camellias need proper water, soil care, and occasional treatment for magnesium deficiencies and premature bud drop.

The article discusses a recent study conducted at the University of Reading, which found that chewing gum can help reduce the likelihood of an earworm (catchy song) recurring in one's mind. The study suggests that this technique could potentially be used to counter unwanted thoughts, although more research is required to confirm its efficacy. Previous research has shown that almost any song can become an earworm, and over 90% of the population experiences them at least once a week, with 15% finding them disturbing.

The study conducted by Swedish and British researchers suggests that consuming two cups of coffee daily could reduce by half the risk of breast cancer reoccurrence in women undergoing treatment with the drug tamoxifen, which is often prescribed to pre-menopausal breast cancer patients. Previous research also indicates a possible link between coffee consumption and reduced risk of certain types of cancer, such as liver cancer and basal cell carcinoma in skin.

No charges have been filed against Jenner for manslaughter, but a wrongful death suit could still be initiated.

1. Neil MacGregor, the director of the British Museum since 2002, has announced his intention to step down at the end of the year, citing it as a difficult decision after 13 years of service.
2. Under MacGregor's leadership, the museum has completed a new building, established partnerships with other museums across the UK and globally, and has been preparing for a new phase that will present diverse histories using the museum's collection.
3. Known for his book and Radio 4 series, A History of the World in 100 Objects, which was inspired by the British Museum's collection, MacGregor expressed excitement for the museum's future, particularly the new Islamic galleries and the future of the Old Reading Room. The museum received 6.7 million visitors in 2014/15, with recent exhibitions focusing on life in China, Afghanistan, and ancient Rome.

At Augusta National Golf Club, a cell phone ban prompted fans to use vintage cameras for photo opportunities, many of whom were navigating these devices for the first time in years. Some were capturing images of golf legends like Tiger Woods, while others were revisiting their old-school gear to produce photos for physical albums or high-quality prints. The experience brought numerous comical moments, as fans grappled with cameras foreign to the digital age.

Allie Davis, a 21-year-old Beyoncé enthusiast in Minneapolis, gave her long-term boyfriend a pop culture-themed exam, involving questions about Beyoncé and other pop stars, to stay in the relationship. He scored 80%, primarily due to questions about Beyoncé's songs. Allie later shared the exam on Twitter, attracting mixed reactions. Despite some criticizing Allie's actions, she described the exam as a playful attempt to entertain herself and her boyfriend.

Ocean photographer Lloyd Meudell specializes in capturing the surreal moment when ocean foam explodes in the air, a sight he calls 'foam surrealism.' He takes most of his shots on beaches in New South Wales, Australia, using an EOS 5D Mark III DSLR and various lenses. Meudell encourages aspiring photographers to familiarize themselves with the ocean's workings, spend time surfing, and start with a GoPro before moving on to more sophisticated equipment, emphasizing the importance of enjoying the process.

Bayern Munich suffered a 3-1 defeat in the first leg of their Champions League quarter-final against Porto, with goals from Ricardo Quaresma (penalty) and Jackson Martinez (2). Bayern manager Pep Guardiola attributed the loss to injuries in his squad, while Porto manager Julen Lopetegui expressed optimism about reaching the semi-finals. Martinez, who returned from injury for the game, was a constant nuisance for Bayern's defense and scored Porto's third goal. Quaresma also praised Porto's teamwork and effort. The return leg will be played next Tuesday in Munich.

The Curiosity Rover has discovered multi-colored veins on Mars at a site called 'Garden City' on Mount Sharp, which could provide insights into Mars' past watery conditions. These mineral veins, containing both bright and dark materials, are believed to have formed billions of years ago due to fluids moving through cracks in the rock. The darker minerals have stumped scientists due to their unique composition. The study by NASA scientists suggests that Mars once had more water than the Arctic Ocean, indicating a potential habitat for life, but over time the planet has lost 87% of its water, leaving it arid and dry. The research is the first to determine the amount of water Mars once contained, with an estimate of at least 12.4 million cubic miles of water during its wet Noachian period.

A 25-year-old man, Carl Bradey, is being hailed as a hero after rescuing a three-year-old girl from a house fire that damaged his body severely, causing horrific burns and permanent nerve damage in his right arm. The fire, which started from a candle, destroyed his rental property and vehicle in Palmerston North, New Zealand. Since the incident, Brarey has endured several major surgeries, including skin grafts and vein removal, and is currently recovering with his mother. His family has established a crowdfunding page to assist him in rebuilding his life. Fire experts remind everyone to use candles cautiously and safely.

1. Thousands of olive trees in the Puglia region of Italy are being cut down due to an outbreak of the xylella fastidiosa bacteria, which has led to a 35% drop in olive oil production and is expected to cause global shortages and price increases.
2. The government's plan to cull around 11 million infected olive trees has been met with protests from growers, who argue that it won't effectively stop the spread of the bacteria.
3. The majority of Italy's olive oil is exported to countries such as the USA, Austria, China, Japan, and Singapore, making the potential loss of production a significant concern for the global olive oil market.

A border guard was killed in a gunfight with militants at the Saudi Arabia-Yemen border, marking the first reported military death for Saudi Arabia since launching airstrikes against Yemeni rebels.
